title: Componentwise abelian structure and exact evaluation for varying-site systems
statement: Let I be a small category, D a VaryingSiteDiagram on I and e a VaryingSiteCoherence on D [def-per-varying-site-system]. Thus D gives small sites, additive exact abelian-sheaf inverse images for arrows, and e specifies their coherent identity and composition isomorphisms. The category S of all coherent systems, with no invertibility condition on its transition maps, admits an abelian structure for which every evaluation ev_i is additive and preserves finite limits and finite colimits. For any arrow h:F→G and kernel fork c, c is limiting if and only if ev_i(c) is limiting for every i. Dually a cokernel cofork is colimiting if and only if each evaluation is colimiting. This statement makes no assertion about injectives, adjoints to evaluation, or complexes.

proof.text: Give compatible Hom families their componentwise abelian group structure, using the additive inverse images supplied by D to prove closure under addition and negation; componentwise composition is bilinear. Construct finite biproducts componentwise. Abelian sheaf categories and their finite limits and colimits exist at every site.

proof.text: For h:F→G form ker(h_i). Finite-limit preservation D.exact_limits identifies the inverse image of each such kernel with the kernel of the inverse-image arrow, so restriction of F.transition gives a unique kernel transition. Cancel the monic inclusions to prove the identity and cocycle laws. Each compatible family into F annihilating h factors componentwise; cancelling those inclusions proves compatibility and uniqueness. This proves the kernel universal property in systems, and the universal-property equivalence for any candidate fork. For cokernels repeat the argument by descent through the epic projections; each inverse image preserves cokernels because its actual sheaf adjunction makes it a left adjoint.

proof.text: Consequently coimage, image and their comparison are componentwise. The component comparisons are isomorphisms in the abelian sheaf categories. Their inverses satisfy the system square by multiplying the original square by inverses, hence give an inverse system map. The coimage-image criterion gives the required Abelian structure. Evaluation preserves the constructed kernels, cokernels and finite biproducts, hence all finite limits and colimits, and is additive by its component formula.

from.place: The passage from finite-stage Leray to the limit spectral sequence in ILO XX 4.4, used in the completion part of proof Step 3 of the blueprint ancestor. Compatible resolutions used before applying continuity, refining the bounded-below derived-sections tool. This node isolates componentwise abelian structure and exact evaluation for varying-site systems, used in the system-resolution argument.

lean.statement: theorem varyingSiteSystem_abelian_componentwise {I : Type u} [SmallCategory I] (D : VaryingSiteDiagram.{u} I) (e : VaryingSiteCoherence D) : ∃ (_ : Abelian (VaryingSiteSystem D e)), ∃ (_ : ∀ i : I, (VaryingSiteSystem.evaluation D e i).Additive), (∀ i : I, PreservesFiniteLimits (VaryingSiteSystem.evaluation D e i) ∧ PreservesFiniteColimits (VaryingSiteSystem.evaluation D e i)) ∧ (∀ (F G : VaryingSiteSystem D e) (h : F ⟶ G) (c : KernelFork h), Nonempty (IsLimit c) ↔ ∀ i : I, Nonempty (IsLimit ((VaryingSiteSystem.evaluation D e i).mapCone c))) ∧ (∀ (F G : VaryingSiteSystem D e) (h : F ⟶ G) (c : CokernelCofork h), Nonempty (IsColimit c) ↔ ∀ i : I, Nonempty (IsColimit ((VaryingSiteSystem.evaluation D e i).mapCocone c)))
